  if (file.exists(p)) { source(p); break }

The components on this page turn shadshiny from a component library into an
application toolkit: a client-side data table, the dashboard shells, and the
flow inputs. The previews are live — sort the table, drag the rating, hold the
stepper — but with no Shiny server attached they won't echo values back.

For the reactive side, see [Data tables](../articles/data-tables.html),
[Dashboards & charts](../articles/charts.html), and
[Forms & validation](../articles/forms.html).

## Data table

`shad_data_table()` is a **bound input**, not an output. It serialises the frame
once and does all sorting, filtering, paging and selection in the browser.
`input$<id>` reports `{selected, sort, filter, page, pageSize}`.

Click a header to sort, Shift+click to add a second sort key, and use the search
box or the per-column filters to narrow the rows.

```{r}
cars <- head(mtcars[order(-mtcars$mpg), c("mpg", "cyl", "hp", "wt")], 8)
cars <- data.frame(model = rownames(cars), cars, row.names = NULL)

demo(
  columns = TRUE,
  shad_data_table(
    "tbl_demo", cars,
    columns = list(
      model = shad_col("Model", width = "12rem"),
      mpg   = shad_col("MPG", format = shad_fmt_number(1)),
      cyl   = shad_col("Cylinders", align = "center"),
      hp    = shad_col("Horsepower", format = shad_fmt_number(0)),
      wt    = shad_col("Weight", format = shad_fmt_number(2, suffix = " t"))
    ),
    selection = "multiple",
    filter    = "global",
    page_size = 5
  )
)
```

### Formatted cells

`shad_col(format=)` takes one of the `shad_fmt_*()` formatters. Each keeps the
**raw** value as the sort key, so a `$1,200.00` cell still sorts numerically and
a formatted date still sorts chronologically.

```{r}
sales <- data.frame(
  order  = c("A-1041", "A-1042", "A-1043", "A-1044"),
  amount = c(1200, 250.5, 89.99, 4300),
  margin = c(0.42, 0.18, 0.31, 0.09),
  date   = as.Date(c("2026-03-01", "2026-03-04", "2026-03-11", "2026-03-15")),
  status = c("paid", "pending", "refunded", "paid"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

demo(
  columns = TRUE,
  shad_data_table(
    "tbl_fmt", sales,
    columns = list(
      order  = shad_col("Order #", width = "8rem"),
      amount = shad_col("Amount", format = shad_fmt_number(2, prefix = "$")),
      margin = shad_col("Margin", format = shad_fmt_percent(1)),
      date   = shad_col("Date", format = shad_fmt_date("%b %d, %Y")),
      status = shad_col("Status", format = shad_fmt_badge(
        c(paid = "default", pending = "secondary", refunded = "destructive")
      ))
    ),
    filter = "none", page_size = 5
  )
)
```

## Value box

`shad_value_box()` is the KPI card. `delta_direction = "auto"` (the default)
reads the sign off the `delta` string, so `"+12.5%"` is up and `"-3%"` is down —
pass `delta_direction` explicitly when the arrow shouldn't follow the sign (a
falling error rate is good news).

```{r}
demo({
  shad_value_box("$45,231", "Revenue", delta = "+20.1%", icon = "credit-card",
                 caption = "vs. last month")
  shad_value_box("2,350", "Subscribers", delta = "+180", icon = "users")
  shad_value_box("0.9%", "Error rate", delta = "-0.4%",
                 delta_direction = "up", icon = "activity",
                 caption = "Lower is better")
  shad_value_box("573", "Active now", icon = "zap", size = "sm")
})
```

## Sparkline

`shad_sparkline()` is a tiny inline chart with no axes, no labels, and no
plotting stack — one SVG path (or a row of bars) that stretches to fill its
box. Every mark is painted with the theme's chart tokens, so the light/dark
switch at the top of this page restyles these in CSS, with no re-render.

```{r}
demo({
  shad_sparkline(c(31, 40, 28, 51, 42, 62, 58, 70), type = "line")
  shad_sparkline(c(31, 40, 28, 51, 42, 62, 58, 70), type = "area")
  shad_sparkline(c(31, 40, 28, 51, 42, 62, 58, 70), type = "bar", color = 2)
  shad_sparkline(c(31, 40, 28, 51, 42, 62, 58, 70), type = "step", color = 3)
})
```

Non-finite values break the series rather than being interpolated across, and
bars hang off a zero baseline once the data crosses it:

```{r}
demo({
  shad_sparkline(c(4, 9, NA, NA, 6, 12, 8), type = "area")
  shad_sparkline(c(-4, -1, 2, 5, -3, 6), type = "bar", color = 4)
})
```

Dropped into `shad_value_box(sparkline = )` it fills the strip at the foot of
the card:

```{r}
demo({
  shad_value_box("$45,231", "Revenue", delta = "+20.1%",
                 sparkline = shad_sparkline(c(31, 40, 28, 51, 42, 62),
                                            type = "area"))
  shad_value_box("2,350", "Subscribers", delta = "+180",
                 sparkline = shad_sparkline(c(12, 19, 15, 27, 24, 31),
                                            type = "bar", color = 2))
})
```

## Mini donut

`shad_mini_donut()` shows a few parts of a whole, with optional content in the
middle. `thickness = 1` gives a pie.

```{r}
demo({
  shad_mini_donut(c(62, 24, 14), center = "62%")
  shad_mini_donut(c(3, 1), size = "5rem", thickness = 0.5)
  shad_mini_donut(c(3, 1), size = "5rem", thickness = 1)
  shad_mini_donut(c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1), size = "5rem")
})
```

## Chart container

`shad_chart_container()` is the card shell around a `plotOutput()` or any
htmlwidget, with an optional legend strip. The stage below holds a static image
in place of a plot, since these pages have no R server behind them.

```{r}
demo(
  columns = TRUE,
  shad_chart_container(
    title = "Revenue by month",
    description = "Jan – Jun 2026",
    legend = TRUE,
    legend_labels = c("This year", "Last year"),
    aspect = "wide",
    shad_skeleton(width = "100%", height = "100%")
  )
)
```

In an app the child is your plot, and `shad_theme_ggplot2()` (or the plotly /
echarts4r equivalents) restyles the figure onto the active palette:

```r
output$plot <- renderPlot({
  shad_current_theme()          # re-render when the theme changes at runtime
  ggplot(df, aes(month, revenue)) +
    geom_col(fill = shad_chart_colors(1)) +
    shad_theme_ggplot2()
})
```

## Timeline

```{r}
demo(
  columns = TRUE,
  shad_timeline(
    shad_timeline_item("Order placed", time = "09:14",
                       description = "Payment authorised.", icon = "check"),
    shad_timeline_item("Packed", time = "11:02",
                       description = "Left the fulfilment centre.", icon = "package"),
    shad_timeline_item("In transit", time = "14:30", status = "active",
                       description = "Out for delivery.", icon = "map-pin"),
    shad_timeline_item("Delivered", status = "muted", last = TRUE,
                       description = "Expected today by 18:00.", icon = "home")
  )
)
```

## Stepper

`shad_stepper()` holds the **1-based** index of the active step. `linear = TRUE`
stops the user skipping ahead of the current step.

```{r}
demo(
  columns = TRUE, {
  shad_stepper("wiz", active = 2,
    shad_step("Account", description = "Email and password"),
    shad_step("Profile", description = "Name and avatar"),
    shad_step("Billing", description = "Card details"),
    shad_step("Done", description = "Confirm"))
  shad_stepper("wiz_v", active = 2, orientation = "vertical",
    shad_step("Draft"),
    shad_step("In review", description = "Waiting on a second approver"),
    shad_step("Published", error = TRUE))
})
```

## Tree

`shad_tree_item()` takes the value first, then the label. Nest items to build
branches; `lazy = TRUE` marks a branch whose children arrive later via
`update_shad_tree(children=)`.

```{r}
demo(
  columns = TRUE,
  shad_tree("files", selected = "app.R", selection = "single",
    shad_tree_item("R", "R", icon = "folder", expanded = TRUE,
      shad_tree_item("app.R", "app.R", icon = "file"),
      shad_tree_item("ui.R", "ui.R", icon = "file")),
    shad_tree_item("www", "www", icon = "folder",
      shad_tree_item("style.css", "style.css", icon = "file")),
    shad_tree_item("data", "data", icon = "folder", lazy = TRUE),
    shad_tree_item("README", "README.md", icon = "file"))
)
```

## Rating

```{r}
demo({
  shad_rating("r1", label = "Rating", value = 3)
  shad_rating("r2", label = "Half steps", value = 3.5, half = TRUE)
  shad_rating("r3", label = "Read-only", value = 4, readonly = TRUE)
  shad_rating("r4", label = "Ten stars", value = 7, max = 10, size = "sm")
})
```

## Number input

A text input with hold-to-repeat stepper buttons. `precision` fixes the decimal
places; `min` / `max` clamp the value.

```{r}
demo({
  shad_number_input("qty", label = "Quantity", value = 1, min = 0, max = 99)
  shad_number_input("price", label = "Price", value = 9.99, step = 0.01,
                    precision = 2)
  shad_number_input("dis", label = "Disabled", value = 5, disabled = TRUE)
})
```

## Dropzone

`shad_dropzone()` bridges to a hidden `fileInput()`, so `input$<id>` is the
**standard Shiny files data frame** (`name`, `size`, `type`, `datapath`) — every
`renderTable(input$files)` you already have keeps working.

```{r}
demo(
  columns = TRUE, {
  shad_dropzone("files", label = "Attachments", multiple = TRUE,
                accept = c(".csv", ".xlsx"),
                hint = "CSV or Excel, up to 5 MB each")
  shad_dropzone("avatar", label = "Avatar", accept = "image/*",
                hint = "PNG or JPG, square works best")
})
```

## Form messaging

The pieces `shad_validator()` drives from the server. In an app you rarely place
these by hand — the validator sets them for you — but they're plain components.

```{r}
demo(
  columns = TRUE, {
  shad_form_message("Looks good.", type = "success")
  shad_form_message("Enter a valid email address.", type = "error")
  shad_form_message("This name is already taken.", type = "warning")
  shad_form_counter(214, 280)
  shad_form_summary("errs", errors = c(
    email = "Enter a valid email address.",
    pw    = "Password must be at least 8 characters."
  ))
})
```
